chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Musa ibn 'Umar al-Sayqal, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhal, from a man whose name he mentioned, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding the game (of hunting), the penalty is doubled for the distance between him and the Badanah (a specific measure of game weight/size); but when it reaches the Badanah, there is no doubling of the penalty upon him.

And the Muhrim (person in Ihram), if hunting repeats from him, he is liable for a Fida' (ransom) for each game if his hunting was by way of error and forgetfulness; but if it was deliberate, he is liable for one Jaza' (penalty), and he is from whom Allah takes vengeance. He narrated.

key_terms.الْبَدَنَةُ: A specific measure of game weight/size used in calculating penalties
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.فِدَاءٌ: Ransom or compensation paid for a specific act

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in penalty for accidental versus deliberate hunting while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the graduated structure of *Kaffarah* (expiation) for hunters in Ihram, distinguishing between accidental (*khata'*) and deliberate (*mu'tamid*) acts. It establishes that while repeated accidental hunting incurs separate penalties for each animal, deliberate hunting results in a single penalty, reflecting the principle of divine retribution (*intiqam*) for intentional transgression. The text also details the specific metric for doubling the penalty based on the size of the game relative to a *Badanah* (a year-old camel).
